activity_context.topic_title: Integration by Substitution With Inverse Hyperbolic Functions

feedback.worked_solution:
Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1/12}\frac{2}{1-9{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=2{\int }_{0}^{1/12}\frac{1}{1-(3x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{artanh}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have $(3x)^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=3x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{12}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |

Using the above, we can now write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/12}\frac{1}{1-9{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{1/12}\frac{1}{1-(3x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1/4}\frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1/4}\frac{\text{d}u}{1-{u}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{artanh}⁡u{|}_{0}^{1/4} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{1}{4})-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{artanh}⁡0 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{1}{4})\end{aligned}
$$
